query: Which muscles are specifically involved in the process of expiration?
parent: Explains that abdominal muscles contract to increase intra-abdominal pressure during active expiration.
children: External oblique contraction increases abdominal pressure during forced exhalation.
Internal oblique helps compress the abdomen during active expiration.
Transversus abdominis compresses abdominal contents to raise intra-abdominal pressure.

responses.excerpt: External Oblique: Contracts to pull the ribcage downward and inward (indirectly aiding expiration). ... Internal Oblique: Also helps in pulling the ribcage inward. ... Transverse Abdominis: Contracts to increase abdominal pressure, which helps push the diaphragm upward.

Transverse Abdominis: Contracts to compress the abdominal cavity, helping push the diaphragm upward. ... Oblique Muscles (Internal and External Obliques): Contract to stabilize the abdominal wall and assist in forced expiration.

External and Internal Obliques: Contract to compress the abdominal cavity, further helping to expel air from the lungs. ... Transverse Abdominis: Contracts to increase intra-abdominal pressure, assisting in expiration.

External Oblique: Contracts to pull the ribcage inward and compress the abdominal cavity. ... Internal Oblique: Similarly contributes to abdominal compression. ... Transversus Abdominis: Contracts to increase abdominal pressure, helping push the diaphragm up.

External Oblique and Internal Oblique: Contract to compress the abdominal cavity, helping push the diaphragm upward. ... Transversus Abdominis: Contracts to increase abdominal pressure, assisting in expelling air.

External and Internal Oblique Muscles: Contract to compress the abdominal cavity, further increasing intra-abdominal pressure and aiding in expiration. ... Transversus Abdominis: Contracts to tighten the abdominal wall, assisting in expelling air from the lungs.

External Oblique and Internal Oblique: Contract to compress the abdominal cavity, helping push the diaphragm upward. ... Transversus Abdominis: Contracts to increase abdominal pressure, assisting in expelling air.

Rectus Abdominis: Contracts to push the abdominal organs inward, increasing intra-abdominal pressure and helping expel air from the lungs. ... Transverse Abdominis and Oblique Abdominals (external and internal): These muscles compress the abdominal cavity, further increasing intra-abdominal pressure and assisting in expiration.
